solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Space traveller given nothing to wake up

parts.note: a comet is a body travelling through space
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A wandering celestial body is handed nothing at all as a way to rouse it.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain consciousness after fainting is an idiomatic way of saying to wake up.

clue.text: Presides over academic posts

definitions.meaning: to chair a meeting is to preside over it

explanation.surface: Someone runs the meetings that oversee university professorships.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for leading a meeting, and the noun for professors' positions.

clue.text: Service I have to give street gang

parts.note: Mass is a church service
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A churchgoer insists on handing out a service to a gang on the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: As a noun, 'the massive' is slang, originally Jamaican and British, for a local crew of youths.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban slang uses this word for a loosely organised group of young people, a gang.

clue.text: Cistern is to fail expensively?

definitions.meaning: a show or film that ... flops at great cost

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a water container is a costly flop.
explanation.definitionFit: A water reservoir is a cistern, and a big-budget flop is said to bomb in this way.

clue.text: Closely follow pig, tricked to go inside

indicators.note: the word for tricked is told to enter the word for pig

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
had, as in 'you've been had', means tricked

explanation.surface: An instruction to tail a pig, with a deceived party slipping into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone secretly, as a detective does, is a verb synonym for following closely.

clue.text: Pilot has crashed, ending up here?

indicators.note: crashed suggests the letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A pilot's crash means landing somewhere with doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' rearranges PILOT HAS; the whole clue also describes where an injured pilot would go.
explanation.definitionFit: A crashed pilot would be taken to a place of medical care, which is where they would end up.

clue.text: Finished crossing river in aircraft

indicators.note: the word for finished spans across the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: done means finished

explanation.surface: Having completed a river crossing in a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmanned remote-controlled flying machine is a kind of aircraft.

clue.text: Flowery tribute, recollecting the war

indicators.note: re-collecting means gathering the letters again in a new order

explanation.surface: Floral tribute laid while remembering the war.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of flowers laid at memorials is a floral tribute.

clue.text: Mark an attractive way of speaking

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, a variant of an
cute means attractive
an accent is a manner of pronunciation

explanation.surface: Mark has a charming voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This diacritic is a written mark above a letter, as in café.

clue.text: Scare in spilling poison

indicators.note: spilling sends the letters of these words tumbling out into a new order

explanation.surface: A fright causes someone to spill a toxic substance.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'spilling' rearranges the letters of SCARE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: This element is a classic toxic substance in murder mysteries, an example of a poison.

clue.text: Batsman's total; made with five boundaries?

definitions.meaning: the runs a cricket batsman has made
a boundary hit along the ground ... four runs in cricket, so five of them make twenty, an old word for which is this

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator notes how a batter's runs were made from a handful of boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a boundary is a shot reaching the edge of the field for four runs; five fours make twenty, which is also what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: The tally of runs is a synonym for total, and twenty is the counting sense of the same word.

clue.text: Manage to sustain one collapse

indicators.note: to sustain is to hold up, so the word for manage holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone must cope with keeping one thing from falling down.
explanation.definitionFit: Downfall or decay to destruction, a noun synonym for a collapse.

clue.text: Second weapon demanding attention

parts.note: a trident is a three-pronged spear

explanation.surface: A backup weapon that insists on being noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud, harsh sound insists on being heard, so the adjective means calling out for notice.

clue.text: Kept back to be given new teaching: not right

indicators.note: not says the letter for right is left out

parts.note: retrained means taught again

explanation.surface: A pupil held back a year to be taught afresh, minus the right answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Held on to or kept, as of staff or of a pupil, matches kept back.

clue.text: Swiss pop groups in strips of linen

parts.note: Geneva is a Swiss city
bands are groups of pop musicians

explanation.surface: Pop acts from Switzerland dressed in linen.
explanation.walkthrough: These are the two white strips worn at the neck by some Protestant clergy, named after Calvin's city.
explanation.definitionFit: The clerical collar pieces are white strips of fabric, so the description matches them exactly.

clue.text: Precise purpose, but no prospect of progress here

parts.note: dead as in dead centre means exact
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: An exact goal is set, yet nothing can move forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A road closed at one end leads nowhere, figuratively a situation with no way forward.

clue.text: On tour, the French abandon restraint

parts.note: le is French for the
on a trip means travelling, on tour

explanation.surface: French tourists throw off all restraint on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is in answer order: LE first, then TRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: To go all out without holding back is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Tristan's lover, one deceived by English

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
sold, as in sold a pup, means cheated

explanation.surface: The legendary lover was cheated by an Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish princess of Arthurian legend and Wagner's opera loved Tristan.

clue.text: Run through new canteen doorway

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
new signals the letters of canteen are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone dashes through the newly opened canteen's door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CANTEEN to ENTANCE, and 'through' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A way in to a building is a doorway, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: River bank hides opening of burrow

indicators.note: the word for bank conceals a letter within it

parts.note: a bank of seats is a tier

indicators.note: opening of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A riverbank conceals the entrance to an animal's burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The river flowing through Rome is a named example of a river.

clue.text: Scary film talks

definitions.meaning: to jaw is to chatter at length, so this is talks as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: The shark movie is famously frightening, and jaw is slang for idle chatter.

clue.text: Country lover avoids one bird

indicators.note: avoids tells us the numeral is kept out of the word

parts.note: a swain is a rustic suitor in pastoral poetry
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rustic suitor steers clear of a particular bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' suggests a nation, but the phrase is a pastoral lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-necked waterfowl, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Man shortly dressing formally

indicators.note: shortly says the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: robing is putting on formal robes

explanation.surface: A man, briefly, putting on formal clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name, so it stands as an example of a man.

clue.text: Roosevelt offered this fresh round of cards

parts.note: new means fresh
a deal is one distribution of cards in a game

explanation.surface: A US president's card-table offer of a fresh hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin Roosevelt's programme of 1930s economic reforms, so it is what he offered Americans.

clue.text: Make fun of staff breaking into earnings

indicators.note: the word for staff forces its way inside the word for earnings

parts.note: pay is what one earns
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Mocking the workforce for raiding the wages.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate mockingly is to satirise, a verb synonym for making fun of.

clue.text: Nervous, being nowhere near the centre

definitions.meaning: literally placed at the rim rather than the middle

explanation.definitionFit: Tense people feel jittery, and the phrase literally means sitting at the brink, far from the middle.
